title: Generator config for generate_episode(seed, config, output_dir) and the train-mode team_config
description: Both sections are optional; {} is a clean company with the default settings. Unknown keys at any level are refused with a message naming them. The parser is genesis_audit.shipped.parse_config. Conditions JSON Schema cannot express, also refused with a message: base_currency and foreign_currencies must all differ; Asia/Almaty needs the period start minus head_days on or after 2024-03-01 (the zone was UTC+06:00 before); the counts of all issues together must stay within 0..12; a company that has no place left for a requested error refuses it ('... left to ...'). The seed is a separate argument: a non-negative integer.

generator.description: The company. Every key is optional; an absent key takes its default. null is the same as {}.

base_currency.description: Currency of the books. Minor-unit exponents: KZT, USD, EUR, GBP 2; JPY 0; KWD 3.

foreign_currencies.description: At least one; none equal to base_currency.

timezone.description: A zone without daylight-saving time. Printed offsets: +05:00, +09:00, +04:00, +05:30, -05:00, +01:00, +00:00.

period.description: One month 'YYYY-MM' or one quarter 'YYYY-Qn', years 2000..2100.

ledger_rows.description: Target ledger size; the result is within about fifteen rows of it, never exactly on it, and never outside 200..2000.

head_days.description: Days of records before the period starts.

tail_days.description: Days of records after the period ends. 10 or more leaves more settled invoices near the period end.

inject.description: What the clerk got wrong. Every count is optional and defaults to 0; each family can be switched on alone. The truth type of a sub-kind key is its family's type. null is the same as {}.

duplicate_invoice.description: One obligation recorded as a second invoice record (truth type duplicate_invoice).

payment_allocation.description: A receipt under-applied to its invoice; missing (nothing applied) or partial is drawn from the seed (truth type payment_allocation).

payment_allocation_missing.description: A receipt that names an open invoice with no allocation row at all (truth type payment_allocation).

payment_allocation_partial.description: A receipt applied for more than 0 and less than required (truth type payment_allocation).

fx_mismatch.description: A receipt in another currency translated at a rate the policy does not select; another date's rate or a mistyped rate is drawn (truth type fx_mismatch).

fx_mismatch_date.description: Translated at the fx.csv rate of another date (often the date printed on the receipt) (truth type fx_mismatch).

fx_mismatch_rate.description: Translated at a rate that is on no fx.csv row of the pair and gives an amount no row gives (truth type fx_mismatch).

cutoff.description: An invoice's revenue row posted on another side of the period than its issued_at (truth type cutoff).

interactions.description: Interacting errors, each giving two issues. A bare name draws every parameter from the seed; an object fixes the parameters it names and draws the others from the seed, except that fx_then_allocation without an allocation parameter is always partial (as its bare name always was).

oneOf.title: Interaction 1: cutoff_and_allocation. An invoice posted on the wrong side of a period boundary whose receipt is also under-applied (issues: cutoff, payment_allocation). The case's own example is {"allocation": "partial", "receipt_currency": "foreign"}.
Interaction 2: duplicate_then_cutoff. A duplicate invoice record whose revenue row is also on the wrong side of a period boundary (issues: duplicate_invoice, cutoff).
Extra: fx_then_allocation. A receipt translated at a wrong rate and the recorded amount under-applied (issues: fx_mismatch, payment_allocation).
